goal: Generate one deterministic, lightweight 3D harbor package containing a boat, reef fish, 500–1,000-triangle textured rocks, a small rippled sand terrain, collectible stars, coral placement, and a browser-ready world manifest.
target: Static GLB assets and world JSON consumed by the Crimson Wheeler Three.js portfolio renderer.
selectionReason: The outcome composes licensed coral artifacts from NexusFactory-Kits with deterministic mathematical generators for the remaining harbor assets and layout.

rejectedTypes.reason: No trained model is required for the stylized low-poly target.
The harbor is an authored portfolio environment rather than a reconstruction of a measured reef.

sources.provenance: User-approved top-down quiet harbor concept in the Website implementation request

seedPolicy.algorithm: FNV-1a seed encoding with mulberry32 streams

stages.output: Boat, fish, rock, sand, and star Three.js object groups
stages.validation: Finite indexed geometry, triangle counts, and bounds
Counts, finite transforms, depth bands, and center clearance

stages.output: Binary GLB assets and world JSON
stages.validation: Non-empty files, GLB headers, checksums, and loader smoke test

claims: Fixed inputs reproduce the semantic signature
Every generated GLB is non-empty and loadable
Runtime assets stay within the declared transfer budget
The top-down harbor remains readable across supported viewports

criteria: Boat remains visible below the name
humanReview.authority: User-approved concept plus current-run web visual review

delivery.format: Versioned Factory Kit plus committed GLB, JSON, image, and video outputs

constraints: Initial 3D asset payload remains below 5 MB
No runtime dependency on NexusFactory-Kits or NexusFactory-Studio
Generated site remains a static Next.js export
The existing shader-renderer public API remains compatible
Every rock mesh contains 500–1,000 triangles and valid normal/UV attributes
Every generated surface texture is 256×256 pixels
